relationships.description: The application event carries or is defined by the data object as its payload, so the event cannot be emitted or interpreted without that data structure's schema.
relationships.evidence: The event class or message schema declares the data object type as its payload field, or the event topic's Avro/JSON schema references the data object's definition.

relationships.description: Occurrence of the application event sets off the joint behaviour carried out by the group of components named by the application collaboration, such as a choreographed saga across several services.
relationships.evidence: Every component in the collaboration has a subscriber or consumer configuration bound to the event's topic or channel that starts their coordinated handling, for example in AsyncAPI specs or message-broker subscription config.

relationships.description: Emission of the application event is the start trigger that launches a run of the application process's ordered sequence of steps.
relationships.evidence: A handler annotated as the listener for the event, such as @EventListener, a Kafka consumer, or a workflow-engine start-event definition, invokes the process's entry point or starts the workflow instance.

relationships.description: The application event signals a system state change that initiates the business process carried out by people or roles in the organisation, such as a notification that starts a manual review.
relationships.evidence: A BPMN model or operational runbook names the event as the start event of the business process, or an integration creates a task in the BPM or ticketing system when the event fires.

notes: Triggering an ApplicationCollaboration is semantically wrong: in ArchiMate, triggers links behaviour elements, while a collaboration is active structure. The event should trigger the collaboration's ApplicationInteraction instead. Using depends-on toward a DataObject is also loose; associated-with, or access via the handling process, expresses an event payload more accurately.
